metadata.title: The Direction of Worship
metadata.subtitle: Understanding the Divine Direction of Every Act of Worship
metadata.theme: Every act of biblical worship has a God-given direction. When we misunderstand the direction of worship, we misunderstand the purpose of worship.
metadata.proposition: God designed every act of worship with a specific direction and purpose. Biblical worship becomes richer and more meaningful when we understand where each act is directed and why God gave it.
metadata.sermonQuestion: What direction is each act of worship actually going?

metadata.title: When Jesus Saw the Multitudes
metadata.subtitle: When Jesus Saw, He Had Compassion
metadata.author: Derek Dodd
metadata.seriesTheme: Jesus sees. Jesus has compassion. Jesus acts.
metadata.proposition: Jesus does not merely show us what compassion looks like. His compassion teaches His disciples how to see people, how to respond to people, and how to draw others into compassionate service.
metadata.sermonQuestion: When I look at people, do I see what Jesus sees?

outline.heading: Compassion Sees
outline.statement: Compassion sees people in their true condition.

conclusion.closingStatement: Jesus is compassion and calls us to become compassion.

cei.command: Matthew 9:38 explicitly commands Jesusâ€™ disciples to pray to the Lord of the harvest for laborers. The broader New Testament also commands compassionate character and responsive love.
cei.example: Jesus provides the approved example of moving toward people, seeing their true condition, being moved with compassion, responding appropriately, and drawing disciples into service.
cei.necessaryInference: The harvest must matter to Christâ€™s disciples; sincere prayer requires genuine concern; divine ownership of the harvest does not eliminate human responsibility; compassionate response varies according to actual need; and genuine compassion cannot consistently coexist with deliberate indifference where opportunity, ability, and responsibility exist.

metadata.title: Compassion in Motion
metadata.subtitle: Compassion Provides
metadata.author: Derek Dodd
metadata.proposition: Biblical compassion does not stop at recognizing need. It moves toward appropriate involvement for another person's good, while recognizing that the disciple is not the ultimate source—Christ is.
metadata.sermonQuestion: When the opportunity is there, will I be willing to participate in compassion?
metadata.seriesTheme: Jesus sees. Jesus has compassion. Jesus acts.

seriesProgression.emphasis: We learn compassion by watching Jesus.
We participate in compassion and become compassionate people.

outline.heading: Compassion Accepts the Interruption
outline.summary: Compassion is willing to allow another person's legitimate need to interrupt our plans.

outline.heading: Compassion Accepts Responsibility
outline.summary: Compassion does not merely recognize a need or distance itself from it; it accepts appropriate responsibility and becomes involved.

outline.heading: Compassion Uses What's Available
outline.summary: Human insufficiency is not an excuse for indifference. Compassion faithfully offers what God has already placed within our stewardship.

outline.heading: Jesus Provides
outline.summary: God has already provided the means for the opportunities placed before us. We must honestly recognize that what we possess belongs to God and willingly steward it for His purposes.

metadata.sermonRefrain: Jesus sees. Jesus has compassion. Jesus acts.
metadata.bigIdea: When we give what we have to Jesus, He can do more than we could ever imagine.

conclusion.heading: Compassion Provides
conclusion.summary: The same Jesus who fed the multitude still provides today. He sees the need, provides the means, and uses willing people.
conclusion.seriesObservation: In these Gospel accounts, Jesus and compassion can be spoken of almost interchangeably without changing the movement of the story: Jesus sees, Jesus has compassion, and Jesus acts. We cannot become Jesus, but we can become compassionate.
conclusion.challenge: The opportunity is still there. Will you be willing?

cei.summary: Scripture commands compassionate character and action and provides approved examples to follow. The study did not establish a separate necessary inference beyond what is already explicitly established by command and example.
